tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.

details.reference: In-house specification for Calcium Carbonate DC

tests.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:30

tests.procedure: Weigh 100 mg in a stoppered tube; add 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min, repeat shake/hold once if not dissolved; add 0.9 mL, then 2 mL, then 7 mL solvent with the same shake and hold steps to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved use 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble), then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble.

details.reference: BP (SC IV K.); USP Description and Relative Solubility

tests.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:31

tests.procedure: Identification test 2 (calcium): dissolve about 20 mg in 5 mL acetic acid; add 0.5 mL potassium ferrocyanide solution (solution remains clear); add about 50 mg ammonium chloride; a white crystalline precipitate forms.

details.reagent: potassium ferrocyanide solution: 5.3 g in water to 100 mL
details.reference: BP Appendix VI Qualitative Reactions and Tests, Calcium

tests.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:32

tests.procedure: Identification test 1 (carbonates): addition of acetic acid to 0.1 g of the substance produces effervescence.
tests.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:32

tests.procedure: Acid-insoluble substances: sample 5.0 g mixed with 10 mL water; add hydrochloric acid dropwise with agitation until effervescence ceases; add water to 200 mL and filter; wash the residue with water until the last washing shows no chloride; ignite; weigh the residue.
tests.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:33

tests.procedure: Heavy metals (limit test): test solution 1.0 g dissolved in 5 mL dilute acetic acid until effervescence ceases, diluted to 12 mL with water; add 2 mL buffer pH 3.5. Standard: 1 mL of 20 ppm lead, 2 mL buffer pH 3.5, 1.2 mL thioacetamide reagent, mixed immediately. Examine both after 2 min: any brown colour in the test solution must not be more intense than the reference.
tests.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:34

tests.procedure: Magnesium and alkali metals (gravimetric, main method): mix 1.0 g sample with 35 mL water; add 3 mL hydrochloric acid, heat, boil 1 min; add 40 mL oxalic acid TS rapidly and stir; add methyl red TS and 6 N ammonium hydroxide dropwise to just alkaline; cool; dilute to 100 mL; stand 4 h or overnight; filter; evaporate 50 mL of filtrate in a platinum dish with 0.5 mL sulfuric acid, heat to dryness and ignite to constant weight. % residue = weight of residue / W x 100.

details.note: alternative complexometric method in the STM not transcribed (main method only)

tests.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:35

tests.procedure: Weigh a previously dried and cooled weighing bottle (W0); add 1.000 g sample (W1 = bottle + material); dry in calibrated oven at 200 ± 10 °C for 4 h, cool in desiccator, weigh (W2); repeat drying to constant weight. % loss on drying = (W1 - W2) / (W1 - W0) x 100.
tests.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:36

tests.procedure: Tapped density: weigh an empty dry 10 mL cylinder and set to zero; put the sample into the cylinder to the volume; record the weight of sample (Wt); tapped density = Wt / Vol. (volume of sample).

details.reference: In-house specification for Calcium Carbonate DC

tests.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:37

tests.procedure: Assay (complexometric titration): dissolve 0.150 g sample in 3 mL dilute hydrochloric acid and 20 mL water; boil 2 min; cool; dilute to 50 mL with water; add 6.0 mL strong sodium hydroxide solution and about 200 mg calconcarboxylic acid triturate; titrate with 0.1 M sodium edetate from violet to full blue. 1 mL of 0.1 M sodium edetate = 4.008 mg Ca. Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100) / Wt.

details.solution: 3 mL dilute hydrochloric acid + 20 mL water, boiled 2 min, diluted to 50 mL
details.equivalenceFactor: 1 mL of 0.1 M sodium edetate = 4.008 mg Ca
details.formula: Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100) / Wt; E.P = end point volume, eq.wt = equivalent weight of calcium (Ca), F = titrant factor, Wt = sample weight (mg)
details.reference: BP Appendix VIII D. Complexometric Titrations

tests.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:38

tests.procedure: Total aerobic microbial count: 10 g sample dissolved in SCDB to 100 mL, mixed continuously; within 1 h pipette 1 mL into each of 4 plates (2 SCDA, 2 SDA); SCDA incubated 48-72 h at 30-35 °C; CFU/g = (sum of colonies on the 2 SCDA plates / 2) x DF (10); no growth reported as 'less than 10' at 1:10 dilution.
tests.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:39

tests.procedure: Total yeasts and molds count: same preparation as TAMC; 2 SDA plates incubated 5-7 days at 20-25 °C; CFU/g = (sum of colonies on the 2 SDA plates / 2) x DF (10).
tests.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:39

tests.procedure: Escherichia coli: incubate the prepared SCDB at 30-35 °C for 18-24 h; transfer 1 mL to 10 mL MacConkey broth (MBP), incubate at 42-44 °C for 24-48 h; subculture on MacConkey agar (MAR) at 30-35 °C for 18-24 h; confirm by Gram stain (gram-negative short rods), EMB (dark-centred colonies) and TBX at 42-44 °C for 18-72 h (blue or green colonies); optional identification system, report present if probability above 70%.
tests.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:40

tests.procedure: Salmonella spp.: transfer 1 mL from the incubated SCDB to 10 mL Rappaport Vassiliadis broth (RVS), incubate 30-35 °C for 18-24 h; subculture on XLD, BGA or HEA at 30-35 °C for 24-48 h; suspect colonies confirmed by Gram stain and TSI slant (alkaline red slant, acid yellow butt, with or without H2S blackening); optional identification system, report present if probability above 70%.
tests.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:41

openQuestions.question: NO ITEM in the app. STM-RM-142 is also the STM number of Calcium Carbonate MD (a different material). Written to STM-RM-142-DC.json as instructed; itemCode is the STM number STM-RM-142, which Calcium Carbonate MD also uses. Confirm the item and the code before loading.
openQuestions.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:5

openQuestions.question: Minimum sample quantity: the spec sheet gives 100 g routine; the STM gives 220 g for routine testing and retention and 120 g for periodic retest. Routine 100 g taken from the spec sheet (per the rule), retention 220 g from the STM; confirm the routine quantity.
openQuestions.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Specifications sheet Calcium Carbonate DC.txt:25; Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:43

openQuestions.question: Assay: the STM formula gives 'eq.wt = Equivalent Weight of Calcium (Ca)', so the result appears to be calcium content, while the spec states NLT 90% without a basis. Confirm whether the result is % calcium or % calcium carbonate, and the unit of Wt (sample given as 0.150 g, formula says mg). Result basis set to PercentAsIs (held as stated).
openQuestions.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:38; Calcium Carbonate DC__Specifications sheet Calcium Carbonate DC.txt:18

openQuestions.question: The 0.1 M sodium edetate titrant has no preparation or standardization in this STM; the titrant factor F cannot be checked from the document.
openQuestions.source: Calcium Carbonate DC__Calcium Carbonate DC-SM - Micro.txt:38

openQuestions.question: Tapped density: the spec sheet technique is 'Tapping', but the STM procedure has no tapping step (it fills a 10 mL cylinder and weighs it). Confirm the procedure.
